formula_checks.name: isBond
formula_checks.why: It reads the one class answer (assetClassOf), so a bond is detected by class as the spec requires; a stated class wins, a maturity date makes a bond, a CD kind makes a bond, and a money-market fund is not a bond (owner, 2026-08-04). It inherits the property-name fault recorded under MK-NW-F-008 (a home named 'Bond Street flat' would read as a bond) but has no fault of its own.
formula_checks.rests_on: Spec §2 quoted on the card; owner rule 2026-08-04 via assetClassOf.

formula_checks.name: alternativesSummary
formula_checks.why: It takes whole accounts that pass isAlternative. An alternative held inside an account of another class (options or a bitcoin ETF in a linked brokerage) is left out, and an alternatives account that records its own uninvested cash is counted whole, cash included. Its total therefore differs from the Alternatives line of the class split (MK-NW-F-019 alternativesTotal) for the same household: two formulas for the same thing. It is also handed no overrides, so a rate the person set for a kind (which blendedReturn honours) cannot reach it.
formula_checks.should_be: Total = the Alternatives part of each account's class split (the same figure as alternativesTotal); blended rate = each Alternatives part x the yearly rate for what it is (the person's own rate for the kind where set, else the benchmark), / that total; growth = total x rate; no figure when the total is 0. Kept private-equity and hedge-fund rows stay in at their benchmark (owner 2026-10-06 keeps the row).
formula_checks.rests_on: MK-NW-F-029/MK-NW-F-027 (the class split adds to everything owned); MK-NW-F-034 (own rate first); ordinary arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: incomeBearingClassOf
formula_checks.why: The order follows the owner's 2026-08-04 rule: money market (words, mmkt/mmf, fund tickers) goes to Stocks / Funds before sweep/settlement, and Treasury-bill fund tickers go to Bonds & CDs. Two faults remain. (1) 'put or call' as whole words sends an equity ETF whose broker name carries 'covered call' (e.g. 'GLOBAL X NASDAQ 100 COVERED CALL ETF') to Alternatives. (2) The commodity and bond words fire on any name, and the company exemption covers only commodity words: a home labelled 'Silver Lake house' or 'Gold Coast condo' reads as Alternatives, and 'Bond Street flat' as Bonds & CDs. Because assetClassOf reads the name (step 3) before the kind (step 4), that house leaves Real estate (realEstateTotal, isRealAsset) and the flat becomes a bond (isBond), so a household sees a wrong number.
formula_checks.should_be: Read put/call as option evidence only with an option shape (an OCC code, a strike or an expiry date); 'covered call', 'ETF', 'fund' or 'trust' in the name is a fund. Name evidence must not override a property or vehicle: return nothing for a property account's name (or have assetClassOf read the kind home/real estate/vehicle and the PROPERTY bucket before the name). Apply the company exemption to bond and Treasury words too.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner rule 2026-08-04 (DEC on cash); ordinary reading of broker security names; assetClassOf step order.

formula_checks.name: realEstateUseOf
formula_checks.why: Owner rule 5 (2026-10-04) makes a property a rental only when a rent entry on the Income screen names it, and a second or vacation home otherwise; propertyUses reads it that way. This function is not handed the income entries and returns the stored use. So (a) a property stored as 'rental' with no rent entry is returned as rental, where the owner says second home; (b) a property with no use stated that a rent entry names is returned as the home when it is the household's only or first-entered property (and as the home when asked alone), so earmarkDefault gives it 0% instead of 100%; (c) a property stored as 'primary' that a rent entry names stays 'primary', where propertyUses says RENTAL. Its own summary of primaryHomeIdOf ('none marked and no use stated on any') also disagrees with primaryHomeIdOf's formula ('among the non-rentals').
formula_checks.should_be: Return propertyUses' answer for the property: rental when an Income-screen rent entry names it; else home when it is the one marked home (or, with no property marked as anything, the one entered first); else second home; land as stated. No household handed in is not a reason to call it the home when the rent entries say otherwise.

formula_checks.name: primaryHomeIdOf
formula_checks.why: (1) It decides 'not a rental' from the stored use, not from the Income screen as owner rule 5 and propertyUses require, so a property with no use stated that a rent entry names can be returned as the home (earmark 0% instead of 100%). (2) 'Entered first' is read as the last in the list, resting on an author claim that the list is kept newest first; primaryCarIdOf reads 'made first' as the lower id. Two definitions of the same thing; if the list is ever handed in another order the home changes. (3) With one property stated rental and one with no use, it names the second as home, while propertyUses applies the first-entered fallback only when no property is marked as anything else; and realEstateUseOf's own summary says the same as propertyUses. The three cards disagree.
formula_checks.should_be: Take rentals from the Income-screen rent entries (propertyUses). Fall back to the first-entered property by one recorded key (created date or id order, the same key primaryCarIdOf uses), not list position. State one rule for 'a rental is marked and another property has no use' and use it in propertyUses, primaryHomeIdOf and realEstateUseOf alike.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner rule 5 (2026-10-04); MK-NW-F-107 propertyUses; MK-NW-F-031 primaryCarIdOf.

formula_checks.name: isRealAsset
formula_checks.why: Real estate or personal property by the single class answer is what it is for. It inherits the property-name fault in MK-NW-F-008 (a home named 'Silver Lake house' reads as Alternatives) but has none of its own.

formula_checks.name: totalAssets
formula_checks.why: Adding every balance is right, and a negative (overdrawn) balance correctly nets down. But 'a missing balance counts as zero' turns an account whose value was never entered into $0, and the total is shown as if complete: the 'missing counted as zero' shape.
formula_checks.should_be: Add every balance; when any account has no balance, give no total (a dash) and name the account(s) without a value, or show the known sum clearly marked as leaving those out. Never treat the gap as $0.
formula_checks.rests_on: Brief rule: 'No answer is a valid answer'; ordinary arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: equitiesTotal
formula_checks.why: It is the Stocks / Funds line of the class split, so a mixed account gives only its fund part and a money-market fund counts here (owner 2026-08-04). It inherits MK-NW-F-008's covered-call fault (such an ETF would land in Alternatives) but adds none.

formula_checks.name: fixedIncomeTotal
formula_checks.why: It is the Bonds & CDs line of the class split; maturity-dated instruments, CDs and T-bill funds count, money-market funds do not (owner 2026-08-04). It inherits MK-NW-F-008's 'Bond Street flat' fault but adds none.

formula_checks.name: alternativesTotal
formula_checks.why: It is the Alternatives line of the class split, so options and crypto ETFs inside a brokerage count and an alternatives account's own cash does not. It inherits MK-NW-F-008's faults (a covered-call ETF or 'Silver Lake house' would land here) but adds none.

formula_checks.name: realEstateTotal
formula_checks.why: The Real estate line of the class split, gross of mortgages, is what it is for. A REIT fund stays in Stocks / Funds; land and property with no kind count. It inherits MK-NW-F-008's 'Silver Lake house' fault but adds none.

formula_checks.name: accountLastFour
formula_checks.why: Digits-only then last four handles '••4821', dashes and spaces correctly, and gives nothing for fewer than four digits. But 'from the mask, or failing that its account number' does not say whether a mask with fewer than four digits ('x-12') counts as failing. Read literally (mask present, so the number is never read) it returns nothing although the account number holds the four digits.
formula_checks.should_be: Use the mask when it yields four or more digits; otherwise use the account number when it yields four or more; otherwise nothing.
formula_checks.rests_on: Card purpose: null only when we genuinely don't have them.

formula_checks.name: accountDisplayName
formula_checks.why: The kind word for a tax-advantaged 'Brokerage' (Roth when tax-free, 401(k) / IRA when tax-deferred) keeps the wrapper visible. But a tax-advantaged account whose kind is missing gets no kind word, so with digits it reads 'Institution -last four' and the wrapper vanishes, against the card's own 'a tax-advantaged account always shows what it is'. 'With none of those ... with the institution in front' is self-contradictory as worded (no institution, yet one in front); and 'the mask at the end only if not already there' does not say whether a name already holding the digits ('Chase Checking 4821') counts.
formula_checks.should_be: When the account is tax-advantaged (tax treatment tax-free/tax-deferred or bucket ROTH/PRE_TAX) and its kind is missing or only 'Brokerage', derive the word from the treatment. State the no-institution branch plainly, and treat the mask as present when its digits already end the name.
formula_checks.rests_on: The card's own stated aim; ordinary reading.

formula_checks.name: earmarkDefault
formula_checks.why: 0% for a 529, the home lived in and the car driven, 100% for the rest follows DEC-0100. Two faults. (1) 'Any unstated property when no household is handed in' cannot be told apart from 'the household has no home': when primaryHomeIdOf returns nothing (e.g. one property stated second home, one with no use), the caller passes undefined and every unstated property gets 0%, while propertyUses and realEstateUseOf call it a second home (100%). (2) A property whose use is stated as the home but which a rent entry names is a RENTAL under owner rule 5 / propertyUses, yet gets 0%.
formula_checks.should_be: Take each property's use from propertyUses: 0% only for the property it names HOME; 100% for rental and second home. Pass 'no home in this household' distinctly from 'no household given'.

formula_checks.name: blendedVolatility
formula_checks.why: It is for the volatility of this portfolio, but a weighted average of the parts' volatilities is that only when every pair moves perfectly together; otherwise portfolio volatility is sqrt(sum_i sum_j w_i w_j s_i s_j rho_ij), which is lower. The card admits this. The Plan's spread of futures is then too wide. 'Else 12%' is also an invented default for a kind the app has no figure for, and the card's purpose says 'class volatility' while its formula uses the kind's.
formula_checks.should_be: Portfolio volatility = sqrt(w' Sigma w) over the earmarked weights, using a stated class correlation table; until that exists, say on screen that the figure is an upper bound, and give no figure for a kind with no volatility rather than 12%.
formula_checks.rests_on: Markowitz (1952) portfolio variance; standard finance practice.

formula_checks.name: blendedReturn
formula_checks.why: An earmark-weighted average of each account's yearly rate is a correct expected return for the nest egg, and it refuses at a zero earmarked total. Its weights come from earmarkDefault, so it carries that card's fault (a second home weighted 0) until MK-NW-F-030 is fixed; an investment account's cash sleeve is rated at the account's kind rate by design.

formula_checks.name: itemising
formula_checks.why: Keep-total = lump, itemised = sum of holdings, remainder = lump - sum is right for ordinary cases. It is silent on two that change what is shown: a listed holding with no value (no price) is summed as if $0, overstating 'not yet explained'; and holdings worth more than the lump give a negative remainder that is not 'still not explained' but an excess.
formula_checks.should_be: Itemised = the priced holdings; when any listed holding has no value, give no remainder and say which holding needs a price. When the sum exceeds the lump, show 'holdings exceed the entered balance by X' instead of a negative unexplained amount.
formula_checks.rests_on: Brief: missing is not zero; parts must match the whole beside them.

formula_checks.name: ledgerGroups
formula_checks.why: By class, a split account's parts go into each class total but the account sits as a row only under its majority class. The rows listed under a heading then do not sum to the heading's total: the Cash heading includes a brokerage's cash but lists only the bank account, and the Stocks heading lists the whole brokerage balance under a smaller total. By institution it is right (trimmed, capitals ignored, first spelling, mix from the same split, largest first) and both views add to everything owned. Silent on a balance split exactly 50/50 between two classes and on an institution of only spaces.
formula_checks.should_be: By class, list a split account under every class it has a part in, showing that part, so each heading equals the rows beneath it; or show the account once with its whole balance and keep heading totals equal to those rows. Say which class wins a tie, and treat a blank institution as No institution set.
formula_checks.rests_on: Brief: parts must add up to the whole they are shown beside; ordinary arithmetic.
